target_customer: Developers and companies that need file upload, transformation and delivery inside their apps
problem: Every web app needs file upload from many sources, and building and maintaining it is tedious.
business_model: Usage-based freemium API with paid Pro and enterprise plans

founders.name: Brett van Zuiden
education: MIT (one of four MIT graduates per TechCrunch)

exit.acquirer: Xenon Ventures (per YC page); later Scaleworks and then Idera (January 2022)

technical_complexity.rationale: A hosted picker with many cloud source integrations, resumable uploads and a CDN needs real integration work, but each piece was known technology.

defensibility.rationale: Developers embedded the SDK and URLs in their apps, which created some switching cost, but competitors and Dropbox style choosers offered similar widgets.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it; it was acquired by a private equity backed owner (Xenon Ventures per YC, then Scaleworks, then Idera in 2022).

market_need_then: By June 2013 the product handled nearly 400 million files per month for about 20,000 apps including SurveyMonkey, Scribd and TED, per TechCrunch.

branding.name_origin: Ink was chosen in 2013 to signal a larger file platform vision; Filestack replaced Filepicker to cover the full tool suite, per the company blog.

rebrands.why: CEO said the new name stood for a larger file management platform vision
Company blog says the picker was only one part of a wider suite of tools; one source gives 2015 and the date is not confirmed by the company

brand_strength.rationale: Three names in three years and no sourced evidence of brand driven growth; the final name is descriptive and fits the product suite.

pivots.to: Ink, a broader file management platform
pivots.why: Wider platform vision per CEO; a Hacker News comment (unverified) says the Ink vision lacked traction and the picker was the profitable product

outcome_analysis: Filepicker grew through developer adoption of a free tier to about 20,000 apps by mid 2013 and raised a 1.8M USD seed from Andreessen Horowitz and Highland. It rebranded twice, then passed to private equity owners, with Xenon Ventures named on the YC page, then Scaleworks and Idera, so it ended as an acquired business rather than a venture scale outcome.
notes: Competitor search returned only current StackShare pages and the TechCrunch launch piece names no rivals, so the competitor list is empty; none dated near the batch was found. Round date is the June 2013 announcement; TechCrunch says the round closed in September 2012. Timing of the Xenon deal conflicts across sources (2013 per an engineer post, 2014 per Xconomy); Xconomy dates Scaleworks to December 2015. Idera acquired Filestack in January 2022 per search coverage of the Idera press release. Founder education taken from TechCrunch stating four MIT graduates and the YC page for Chang; van Zuiden's page shows no bio. The YC directory marks the company Inactive because it was acquired; exit.type acquisition is correct and the conflict is only the directory label.
